answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by charging every new identity a small proof of useful work before it may trade: each agent must solve a fresh, verifiable computation puzzle tied to its key, like cutting a quartz crystal to a unique facet. A lone relic account can afford one puzzle, but a Sybil farmer spawning a nebula of thousands faces the same cost multiplied thousands of times, while honest agents pay it once and reuse the attestation. The work is cheap for one real agent and ruinous at scale.
